disposition: shared fatty acid and pain-reliever restriction
assessment: The whole-walnut and training trial mentions alpha-linolenic acid as a walnut constituent. Pain relievers were restricted for testing. No flaxseed-oil exposure or pain-rating outcome was measured.
SAGE Open Medicine appears in the citation for the SF-36 instrument. The fibromyalgia trial used cannabinoid and comparator oils and reported pain, sleep quality and fatigue. It did not assign sage.

disposition: avocado in mixed placebo and somnolence adverse events
assessment: Table 2 lists three somnolence reports in the placebo and five in the cannabinoid arm. The oil placebo also contained walnut and MCT oils. The outcome concerns adverse events in fibromyalgia. Existing assessment PMID42142029 records this pair.

disposition: avocado in mixed placebo and measured anxiety
assessment: HADS anxiety means in the avocado, walnut and MCT placebo group were 9.40 at baseline and 9.60 after treatment. Between-arm uncertainty includes benefit and worsening. Oil proportions, pressing grade and Parkinson anxiety remain untested.

Table 4 reports separate fatigue domains after cannabinoid oil and the MCT, walnut and avocado placebo blend. The MCT oil has no stated coconut origin or virgin grade. No isolated coconut-oil preparation was assigned.

Table 2 counts somnolence events after cannabinoid and mixed placebo oils. The named MCT carrier has no stated source. The study supplies no virgin-coconut-oil and Parkinson daytime sleepiness estimate.

disposition: sunflower oil diet comparator in aged mice
assessment: Sunflower oil supplied fat in the comparator feed. Open-field activity differed little by group and the authors found no clear intervention effect on stress sensitivity from fecal droppings. Whole-walnut replacement, age and enrichment context preclude an isolated cold-pressed oil or clinical anxiety comparison.

disposition: walnut oil in cited cognitive study
assessment: Walnut oil is mentioned for a distinct experiment on water-maze performance. The current study's feed contained whole walnuts and measured open-field activity and fecal droppings as animal proxies. It provides no administered walnut-oil anxiety contrast.
